title: Amartha 10X Run 2026: A Purple-Hued Half Marathon Debut in the Heart of Senayan
meta_description: Everything to know before entering Amartha 10X Run 2026 in Senayan: course, village vibe, price, cut-offs and whether it's worth your race calendar slot.
dek: A fintech-backed festival race built around Jakarta's iconic GBK loop, now expanding into half marathon territory with a rural-market twist at the finish.
verdict: Amartha 10X Run is less a pure racing test and more a community festival that happens to include a certified 10K and half marathon around Senayan's GBK precinct. Expect a well-stocked race pack, a growing but still young operation, and a genuinely distinctive post-race village themed around Indonesia's grassroots MSME economy. It suits runners who want an accessible city half marathon with a social conscience and a party atmosphere at the finish, rather than those chasing a PB on a stripped-back, competition-first course.

sections.heading: The Course: Senayan's GBK Loop, Now With a Half Marathon Leg
paragraphs: The 2026 edition starts and finishes at Plaza Parkir Timur GBK in Senayan, with runners choosing between 10K and, for the first time on this particular venue configuration, a full 21.1km half marathon [1]. The previous edition ran from Plaza Barat GBK and, according to race-day reporting, stretched out through the wider Senayan and SCBD corridor toward Bundaran Hotel Indonesia before looping back [4]. That kind of route gives the half marathon distance real variety rather than just laps of the stadium precinct, though it also means runners should expect the usual weekend Jakarta road-closure logistics that come with a course threading through busy commercial districts.

Cut-off times are set at 2 hours for the 10K and 4 hours for the half marathon [2], which is generous enough for most recreational finishers but worth noting if you're a walk-run participant on the longer distance.

sections.heading: Growing Pains and Growing Numbers
paragraphs: This is still a young event finding its scale. The organisers expanded the field from roughly 3,000 participants in the inaugural year to more than 5,200 runners in 2025, alongside adding the half marathon and a Kids Dash category for the first time [11][12]. That kind of year-on-year jump is a good sign of demand, but it also means the operational template — start corrals, aid stations, road marshalling — has had to scale quickly rather than being battle-tested over many editions.

Race Director Satrio Guardian of Indonesia Muda Road Runner, the executing partner, has been vocal about applying international-standard event management to keep participants safe and comfortable [22]. Post-event reporting from the 2025 edition described the day as having gone smoothly, with organisers crediting collaboration across sponsors and the running community for pulling it off [26].

sections.heading: Logistics: What's in the Bag and When to Collect It
paragraphs: Registration for 2026 opens with prices starting from IDR 450,000, and every entrant is set to receive a race jersey, bib with timing chip, finisher medal, race bag, event insurance, and sponsor products bundled into the package [1][2]. Race Pack Collection is scheduled for Friday and Saturday, 4–5 September 2026, ahead of Sunday's race day [2].

Past editions have pulled in a solid sponsor roster spanning apparel, hydration, wearables and hospitality brands, including names like Reebok, Pocari Sweat, Decathlon, Coros and Aryaduta Hotel [28], which tends to translate into decent freebies and activation booths on-site rather than just a bare-bones bib collection.

sections.heading: The Atmosphere: A Running Festival With a Social Mission
paragraphs: What sets Amartha 10X Run apart from a typical city road race is the finish-line experience. The 2025 edition's Race Village was built around a rural-market concept, letting finishers play traditional games, sample products from Amartha-backed micro-enterprises, and even take home produce and betta fish as symbols of grassroots resilience [22]. It's an unusual and genuinely memorable touch for a road race, tying the event directly to Amartha's underlying business as a microfinance platform supporting women-led MSMEs across tens of thousands of Indonesian villages [25].

The event also leans into a strong visual identity — 2025's edition was awash in purple branding across the GBK-to-SCBD corridor [24] — and organisers have described cheering points staffed by mothers connected to Amartha's partner network, meant to echo the tenacity of the entrepreneurs the brand supports [21]. For 2026, Amartha has gone further still, tying limited-edition VIP race access — including lounge access, a priority lane at pack collection and complimentary medal engraving — to minimum investments in its Amartha Prosper microfinance product [32], a genuinely unusual crossover between race perks and fintech marketing that prospective entrants should be aware of even if it isn't required for standard entry.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a fast, no-frills PB course, this probably isn't it — the appeal here is the festival wrapper, the finish-line market, and the feel-good branding around supporting Indonesian MSMEs, not a stripped-down competitive half marathon [22]. But if you're after an accessible city half marathon debut or a sociable 10K with a distinctive post-race experience, a growing field size, and a reasonably well-stocked entry package from IDR 450,000, it's a solid pick on the Jakarta calendar [1][2].

First-timers to the half marathon distance may appreciate the generous 4-hour cut-off, while returning finishers should note that with entrant numbers climbing fast each year, this is an event still scaling up its infrastructure — worth bearing in mind for expectations around start-corral crowding and aid-station queues on race day [11].
